project.name: hust-foodmap
project.description: A food discovery application for HUST students, with an independent Next.js and React frontend and NestJS backend in an npm workspace sharing TypeScript data types. The frontend provides search, filters, a sidebar, and an interactive map. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Purpose And Boundaries
tour.description: Start with the workspace overview to understand campus restaurant discovery and the Next.js frontend plus NestJS API architecture. The guidelines establish server and client responsibilities, desktop map expectations, and the requirement to label sample data and local trial features.

tour.title: Server Rendered Catalog Entry
tour.description: The discovery page requests its initial catalog from the server loader before handing the result to the interactive client boundary. The cached loader keeps the backend origin private, uses a request timeout, and returns a recoverable null result when the API is unavailable.

tour.title: Recoverable Browser Catalog
tour.description: CatalogClient turns the server result into ready, loading or error states and supports an abortable retry. The shared status shell and route loading or error components give the page consistent feedback before the restaurant discovery interface mounts.

tour.title: Retry Through The Proxy
tour.description: Follow the retry into the browser API client, which validates the response envelope and combines cancellation with a timeout. Next.js rewrites the same-origin API path to the private backend, while environment examples distinguish server settings from public map configuration.

tour.title: Discovery Interaction Coordinator
tour.description: Once a catalog is ready, FoodMap coordinates the sidebar, search, filters, selected restaurant, saved places and local trial meal plans. Its navigation and reusable cards expose those interactions, while responsive food images support both cards and map markers. Saved and planning state use local storage; these trial interactions do not imply implemented booking or account services.

tour.title: Validated Shareable Query State
tour.description: The query hook connects the discovery controls to browser history without refetching server components. The model validates restored URL values, omits defaults when serializing, and filters or sorts restaurants by search, budget, meal duration and viewport. Walking estimates are straight-line or sample-based estimates rather than routed itineraries.

tour.title: Map And User Position
tour.description: The discovery map loads behind the browser-only feature boundary and manages the MapLibre lifecycle, photo markers, clustering and viewport filtering. The map provider chooses configured, public or illustrative offline styles, while the geolocation hook supports retry and stale callback protection. Coordinates remain in memory instead of being written to shared URLs or saved state.

tour.title: Shared Domain Contracts
tour.description: The contracts workspace supplies the restaurant and data-envelope vocabulary used on both sides of the catalog boundary. Its food-group implementation keeps category matching consistent between API and browser filtering. Visit-plan, realtime and service declarations describe future contracts and do not establish implemented endpoints.

tour.title: NestJS Application Bootstrap
tour.description: Now follow the backend dependency chain from main into application creation and module composition. Startup establishes the listener, API prefix, CORS policy, transforming validation and shutdown hooks; the application module connects the restaurant feature and health response. This is the service reached by the server loader and browser proxy.

tour.title: Validated Sample Restaurant API
tour.description: The restaurant controller exposes collection and identifier routes, and the DTO validates query values before the service handles them. The service filters the fixture catalog using shared food groups, normalized search, budget and open status, and reports missing identifiers. The six fixture listings, prices and ratings are illustrative records rather than verified live restaurant data.

tour.title: Workspace And Runtime Preparation
tour.description: The root manifest coordinates development, builds, typechecking and tests across the workspaces. Frontend preparation produces responsive images and copies the MapLibre worker before serving or building. These build assets support the photographs and browser map encountered earlier in the tour.

tour.title: Verification And Integration Limits
tour.description: Finish with the HTTP restaurant tests and the recorded verification guide to connect architectural decisions with evidence. Browser scripts exercise layout, map and discovery interactions, while the guide distinguishes current checks from historical migration evidence and remaining integration limits. These artifacts help a newcomer choose relevant checks before changing the catalog or discovery experience.
